key_insight: Optimization theory better explains practical machine learning when it preserves the actual sketching, clipping, normalization, layer-wise updates, and approximation procedures.
engineering_relevance: Training stability and convergence depend on matching objectives to sampling schemes and jointly tuning clipping schedules, orthogonalization precision, and learning rates.
method: Analyze submodel training bias and incorporate the sketch distribution into the objective for unbiased gradients.
Study adaptive quantile clipping and combine smoothed normalization with error compensation for distributed private optimization.
Develop layer-wise generalized smoothness and the Gluon framework for Muon- and Scion-style methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence guarantees, validation of a layer-wise smoothness model, and an orthogonalization–stepsize tradeoff, but specifies no datasets or numerical results.
watch_item: Fixed-quantile clipping retains bias, and less precise Muon orthogonalization requires smaller stepsizes.
paper_title: Understanding Practical Optimization in Machine Learning
